maintenance.rule_inventory: cases.expected_rules is the independent complete rule inventory. Missing, additional, unchecked or unexpected broken rules fail; do not regenerate expectations from changed configurations.

FreshnessPublication.bounds: Two abstract clock positions (2,3), original validation ticks (1,2,3), one pending request plus one cache return, two generations, two scopes and root/Requires failure targets. Initial prior evidence and the pending ticket are explicit bounded premises.
FreshnessPublication.atomicity: Receive represents synchronous evidence admission and map publication after asynchronous acquisition; original validation evidence is supplied by the CLI. Clock advances and lifecycle cancellation may interleave before either bounded return. This does not model remote acquisition as atomic.

SelectionGraph.bounds: One prior root/Requires vector <1,2>, one replacement <2,1>, separate complete-closure and retained-plus-new working-set budget premises, one prepare, independent checks and one final commit. One generation change can be caused by explicit release while acquisition is pending.

SelectionGraph.atomicity: Prepare, identity validation, output budget validation and final guarded commit are separate steps. Commit is synchronous. In deferred Pi the approved graph remains staged until the provider hook; this model's selected vector denotes the approved fixed selection, not provider acceptance or durable activation.

DeliveryBoundary.bounds: A previously validated selected root v2/Requires v1 graph; one initial request, at most one retry after discarded drafts, one lifecycle event among cancel/switch/rewind, and one current branch plus its rewind. Full/partial and exact/mismatched identity, response and turn outcomes are finite scenarios. Explicit release retires this root's effective projection and advances the request generation; the historical provider acceptance remains distinct.
owners: final-request.ts assessFinalRequestPayload/createFinalRequestLedger; concrete request roles and entity digests outside finite variables
session-graph.ts applyRootRelease; host-skills.ts notion_ctl working_set release resets pending graphs/candidates and advances generation
DeliveryBoundary.atomicity: Headers, turn completion, draft return, host apply/drop and later public projection acknowledgement are separate transitions. A 2xx response proves request acceptance and may record active delivery before stream completion. A later failed turn does not erase that historical acceptance. No draft is a persisted projection until observed in the public branch.
replays: session-active.test.ts selected/partial inactivity, discarded drafts, failed/aborted/late/rewound deliveries

RecoveryClosure.bounds: Three sequential prompts; roots A and C share mandatory B, independent D; original bytes present or B missing; current authority revisions 1/2; business disablement, one observed access denial and one retired restore ticket. The model does not manufacture remote historical bytes.
owners: session-recovery.ts fixed restoration, closure isolation and bounded retry
index.ts restoreActive source acquisition and original snapshot checks
host-skills.ts fixed-restoration observations and final context publication
RecoveryClosure.atomicity: Restore start, SDK completion, final closure/permission projection and next prompt are separate transitions. Current Notion edits and observed denial may interleave before projection. An epoch change cancels this operation; it cannot publish old bytes. A failed fixed read becomes a local capability warning, not a persistent prompt abort.
RecoveryClosure.fairness: Weak fairness for local start/restore completion/projection and supplying the next prompt. Assumes every external acquisition terminates with bytes, failure, timeout or cancellation. ConversationCanContinue proves that all three prompts can reach a provider request or explicit cancellation under those assumptions; it does not prove arbitrary provider completion, model task quality, UI input, or eventual Notion availability.
replays: session-recovery.test.ts: actual index hooks for missing snapshots, business-disabled originals, shared Requires and independent roots
session-recovery.test.ts: permission/cancellation during restore and repeated prompts

excluded: SDK transport and decoder implementation, installed CLI/SDK version and package hashes, management command observation and catalog invalidation, prompt guidance and actual Pi/provider runs are outside the finite state model. Selected content pins mean locally verified immutable content. They do not promise remote historical recovery, create Notion history, or extend current permission evidence.

Source/target identity, wall-clock behavior, HTTP consistency and serialized provider bytes retain their concrete test obligations; finite exploration does not prove arbitrary production interleavings.
